name: Caijia
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Lu [Lü], Shanshan. 2020. A Reference Grammar of Caijia: An unclassified language of Guizhou, China. Thèse de doctorat, École des hautes études en sciences sociales (EHESS), Paris (dir. Hilary Chappell). NNT 2020EHES0082, 684 pp. (open thesis via theses.fr; published revision = Lü 2022, De Gruyter Mouton, DOI 10.1515/9783110724806).
catalog_locator: Thesis p. 9 (Ch. 1 §IV 'Basic features'); Ch. 2 'Sound system' pp. 17-53: intro p. 17, §IV 'Tones' pp. 44-45, p. 51, conclusion p. 53; Ch. 10 §II.2 'Completive [VP ha⁵⁵]' p. 326.
catalog_quote: [p. 9] First, featuring less developed morphology, i.e. lacking inflectional and with a small inventory for derivational types of morphology, Caijia is a typical analytic, tonal language. [p. 17] This chapter aims at giving a brief description of the sound system of the Caijia language and will not explore its phonological system in depth. [pp. 44-45] ...there are several citation forms bearing the low-level tone 22. Therefore, there are in total five tones in Caijia. Five citation tones: High-level (H): 55 ɔ⁵⁵ 屋 ‘house’ / Mid-level (M): 33 mɛ³³ 马 ‘horse’ / Low-level (L): 22 ɔ²² 这 ‘this’ / Low-falling (LF): 21 ɔ²¹ 留 ‘stay’ / High-rising (HR): 24 mɛ²⁴ 蛙 ‘frog’. [p. 51] Apart from these unpredictable patterns, prosodic factors such as intonation and stress can definitely affect the surface tone of a morpheme. As shown in the example below, two tonal forms are observed for the word ‘pat’. ... The first pʰa³³ ‘pat’ has a lower pitch than the second one, probably because it is situated in the sentence final position of a declarative. Alternatively, the second pʰa⁵⁵ pitches high is probably due to stress. [p. 53] Five citation tones are observed, but there are only four surface tones. Examples are given to show that tone sandhi certainly exists in Caijia, but only the clearly evident sandhi rules are given at present. [Ch. 10, completive] It should be mentioned that ha⁵⁵ is often stressed in a sentence and the tone value is often [51] when it is stressed.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Caijia (Xingfa variety) is described as a lexical-tone language: five citation tones (55, 33, 22, 21, 24), four surface tones, tone sandhi and derivational tone change. The grammar gives no word-stress placement rule and no section on stress/accent; stress is mentioned only as a sentence-level prosodic factor that can raise the surface pitch of a morpheme (pʰa 'pat'; completive ha⁵⁵ realised [51] 'when it is stressed').
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes: low-level /22/ usually surfaces as [21]; /33/ -> [21] before /55/ obligatorily; free variation /33/~[21] after /55/ and /21/~[33] before /21/; plural pronouns and diminutives derived by tone change to [24].
new_statements.domain_note: The two stress remarks concern emphasis within sentences/connected texts, not lexical word stress; citation forms are monosyllabic tone-bearing morphemes. Author explicitly says the chapter is 'a brief description of the sound system' and does not explore phonology in depth.
new_statements.identity_note: Lü 2020/2022 describes the Xingfa 兴发乡 variety of Hezhang County (with occasional notes on the Weining/Xinfa variety); Hsiu 2018 describes the Niujiaojing (Yangjie, Weining) dialect. All are caij1234 (no sub-glottocodes). Caijia has no ISO code.

tone_statements.quote: 兴发乡蔡家话有四个声调，如 55、24、33、31。松林坡蔡家话也有四个声调：... 55 pɪi55 头发 ɕi55 刀 kv̩55 脚 35 mi35 猫 ɡa35 茄子 ŋu35 我们 33 zɿ33 雨 kʰĩ33 天 ɯ33 衣服 21（221） ne21 水牛 tu21 桌子 ɣan21 有 ① 21 有时实现为 221。② Lü Shanshan（2022：37）已指出，蔡家话也有连读变调。尽管笔者已观察到一定的变调现象，如 21 调在复合词等环境中多读为 22 调。... 由于本文调查范围有限，对连读变调的系统考察尚有待进一步开展。
tone_statements.translation: Xingfa Township Caijia has four tones, e.g. 55, 24, 33, 31. Songlinpo Caijia also has four tones: 55 (pɪi55 'hair', ɕi55 'knife', kv̩55 'foot'), 35 (mi35 'cat', ɡa35 'eggplant', ŋu35 'we'), 33 (zɿ33 'rain', kʰĩ33 'sky', ɯ33 'clothes'), 21 (221) (ne21 'buffalo', tu21 'table', ɣan21 'have'). (1) 21 is sometimes realised as 221. (2) Lü Shanshan (2022: 37) has pointed out that Caijia also has tone sandhi. The author has observed some sandhi, e.g. tone 21 is mostly read as 22 in compounds and similar environments. ... As the scope of this survey was limited, a systematic study of tone sandhi remains to be done.
tone_statements.locator: p. 207, §2.2.5 声调; '..' after the colon elides footnote marker 11
tone_statements.summary: Four tones, Chao values 55, 35, 33, 21 (at times 221), from fieldwork with one speaker; sandhi 21>22 in compounds; fn. 11 cites Lü 2022's five categories (55, 33, 22, 21, 24). Word list tone-marked.
